title: Nuevo Laredo student takes cactus-based 'Nopalskin' to national science expo
excerpt: José Ángel Rangel, a first-year secondary student at Colegio San José de Nuevo Laredo, is representing Tamaulipas at ExpoCiencias Nacional 2026 in Monterrey with Nopalskin, a bioplastic-like material made from nopal cactus.
content:
A student from Nuevo Laredo is representing Tamaulipas at the ExpoCiencias Nacional 2026 in Monterrey with an ecological invention made from cactus, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

José Ángel Rangel, a first-year secondary school student at Colegio San José de Nuevo Laredo, developed Nopalskin, a bioplastic-like material made from nopal cactus mucilage, combined with natural latex and biodegradable pigments.

The material is intended as a sustainable alternative to plastic bags and wrappers, with the project aiming to reduce plastic use and improve care for the environment, including in the border region, El Mañana reported.

ExpoCiencias Nacional 2026, held at Cintermex in Monterrey, Nuevo León, began on Tuesday, Nov. 11, brings together about 1,500 young people from across Mexico, and concludes with an awards ceremony on Saturday, Nov. 14, according to the report.

Nopalskin previously won first place at both the local and state levels in the Certamen Estatal de Creatividad e Innovación Tecnológica en Tamaulipas, in the youth category, before advancing to the national expo.

Source: El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, Nov. 12, 2026.
